audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Stephen's Israel history speech, Abraham/Joseph/Moses/temple critique, resistance to Spirit, Son of Humanity vision, Stephen's death, Saul witness.

verses.restored: The high priest said, Are these things so?

familiar.text: Then said the high priest, Are these things so?

modern.text: Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”

original.text: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· ⸀Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;

verses.restored: He said, Men, siblings and fathers, hear. The Divine of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,

familiar.text: And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,

modern.text: And Stephen declared: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν,

verses.restored: and said to him, Go out from your land and your kindred, and come into the land that I will show you.

familiar.text: And said unto him, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.

modern.text: and told him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ⸀ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς ⸀τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.

verses.restored: Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. From there, after his father died, the Divine moved him into this land in which you now live.

familiar.text: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.

modern.text: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him out of that place and into this land where you are now living.

original.text: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν. κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε,

verses.restored: He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a footstep, yet promised to give it to him for possession and to his seed after him, though he had no child.

familiar.text: And he gave him none inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on: yet he promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.

modern.text: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.

verses.restored: The Divine spoke thus: his seed would be a sojourner in another land, and they would enslave and mistreat them four hundred years.

familiar.text: And God spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

modern.text: God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

original.text: ἐλάλησεν ⸀δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·

verses.restored: And the nation they serve I will judge, said the Divine, and after these things they will come out and serve me in this place.

familiar.text: And the nation to whom they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: and after that shall they come forth, and serve me in this place.

modern.text: ‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’

original.text: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ⸀ἐὰν ⸀δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ⸂ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν⸃, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.

verses.restored: He gave him the covenant of circumcision; and thus Abraham fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, Isaac Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

familiar.text: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so Abraham begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

modern.text: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs. Joseph Sold into Egypt (Genesis 37:12–30)

original.text: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, ⸀καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, ⸁καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.

verses.restored: The patriarchs, jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt; and the Divine was with him,

familiar.text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but God was with him,

modern.text: Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him

original.text: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: and rescued him from all his pressures, gave him grace and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his house.

familiar.text: And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.

modern.text: and rescued him from all his troubles. He granted Joseph favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.

original.text: καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον ⸀καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: A famine came upon all Egypt and Canaan, and great pressure, and our fathers were finding no food.

familiar.text: Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.

modern.text: Then famine and great suffering swept across Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could not find food.

original.text: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν ⸀Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: Hearing there was grain in Egypt, Jacob sent our fathers first.

familiar.text: But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.

modern.text: When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα ⸂σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον⸃ ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·

verses.restored: On the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became manifest to Pharaoh.

familiar.text: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph’s kindred was made known unto Pharaoh.

modern.text: On their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh.

original.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ⸀ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ ⸀γένος Ἰωσήφ.

verses.restored: Joseph sent and called Jacob his father and all the kindred, seventy-five souls/lives.

familiar.text: Then sent Joseph, and called his father Jacob to him, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.

modern.text: Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all. Israel Oppressed in Egypt (Exodus 1:8–22)

original.text: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο ⸂Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε,

verses.restored: Jacob went down into Egypt, and he died, he and our fathers.

familiar.text: So Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he, and our fathers,

modern.text: So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.

original.text: ⸂καὶ κατέβη⸃ Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον. καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν,

verses.restored: They were carried over to Shechem and placed in the tomb Abraham had bought for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

familiar.text: And were carried over into Sychem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmor the father of Sychem.

modern.text: Their bones were carried back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a price he paid in silver.

original.text: καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ⸀ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ⸀ἐν Συχέμ.

verses.restored: As the time of the promise drew near, which the Divine had confessed to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,

familiar.text: But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which God had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,

modern.text: As the time drew near for God to fulfill His promise to Abraham, our people in Egypt increased greatly in number.

original.text: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ⸀ὡμολόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ,

verses.restored: until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

familiar.text: Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.

modern.text: Then another king, who knew nothing of Joseph, arose over Egypt.

original.text: ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ⸂ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον⸃, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.

verses.restored: This one dealt craftily with our kin and mistreated the fathers, making them expose their infants so they would not be kept alive.

familiar.text: The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.

modern.text: He exploited our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would die. The Birth and Adoption of Moses (Exodus 2:1–10; Hebrews 11:23–29)

original.text: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς ⸀πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν ⸂τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα⸃ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζῳογονεῖσθαι.

verses.restored: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful to the Divine; he was nourished three months in his father's house.

familiar.text: In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months:

modern.text: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in the sight of God. For three months he was nurtured in his father’s house.

original.text: ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·

verses.restored: When he was exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and raised him as her own son.

familiar.text: And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.

modern.text: When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.

original.text: ⸂ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν⸃ ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.

verses.restored: Moses was educated in all the wisdom of Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and works.

familiar.text: And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.

modern.text: So Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action. The Rejection and Flight of Moses (Exodus 2:11–22)

original.text: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη ⸀Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When forty years of time were fulfilled for him, it came up upon his heart to visit his siblings, the children of Israel.

familiar.text: And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.

modern.text: When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταετὴς χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: Seeing someone being wronged, he defended him and made justice for the oppressed one, striking the Egyptian.

familiar.text: And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian:

modern.text: And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.

original.text: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.

verses.restored: He thought his siblings would understand that the Divine was giving them salvation through his hand, but they did not understand.

familiar.text: For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.

modern.text: He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.

original.text: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ⸀ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν ⸂σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς⸃, οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.

verses.restored: The next day he appeared to them as they were fighting and urged them toward peace, saying, Men, you are siblings; why do you wrong one another?

familiar.text: And the next day he shewed himself unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?

modern.text: The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’

original.text: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ ⸀συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών· Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ⸀ἐστε· ἱνατί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;

verses.restored: But the one wronging the neighbor pushed him away, saying, Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?

familiar.text: But he that did his neighbour wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?

modern.text: But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφʼ ⸀ἡμῶν;

verses.restored: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?

familiar.text: Wilt thou kill me, as thou diddest the Egyptian yesterday?

modern.text: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’

original.text: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ⸀ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;

verses.restored: Moses fled at this word and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.

familiar.text: Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.

modern.text: At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons. The Call of Moses (Exodus 3:1–22)

original.text: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.

verses.restored: When forty years were fulfilled, a messenger appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.

familiar.text: And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.

modern.text: After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.

original.text: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ⸀ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου·

verses.restored: Moses, seeing it, marveled at the vision; as he approached to observe, the voice of the Lord came:

familiar.text: When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold it, the voice of the LORD came unto him,

modern.text: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to look more closely, the voice of the Lord came to him:

original.text: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ⸀ἐθαύμασεν τὸ ὅραμα. προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ ⸀κυρίου·

verses.restored: I am the Divine of your fathers, the Divine of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. Moses became trembling and did not dare to observe.

familiar.text: Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.

modern.text: ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.

original.text: Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ ⸀καὶ Ἰσαὰκ ⸁καὶ Ἰακώβ. ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.

verses.restored: The Lord said to him, Loose the sandal from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.

familiar.text: Then said the Lord to him, Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground.

modern.text: Then the Lord said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου, ὁ γὰρ τόπος ⸀ἐφʼ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.

verses.restored: Seeing, I saw the mistreatment of my people in Egypt, and I heard their groaning, and I came down to rescue them. Now come, I will send you into Egypt.

familiar.text: I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

modern.text: I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.’

original.text: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα, καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς· καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ⸀ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.

verses.restored: This Moses, whom they denied, saying, Who appointed you ruler and judge? this one the Divine sent as ruler and redeemer with the hand of the messenger who appeared to him in the bush.

familiar.text: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.

modern.text: This Moses, whom they had rejected with the words, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ is the one whom God sent to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.

original.text: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν, ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν, τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ⸀καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ⸂ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν⸃ χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ.

verses.restored: This one led them out, doing wonders and signs in Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the wilderness forty years.

familiar.text: He brought them out, after that he had shewed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.

modern.text: He led them out and performed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.

original.text: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν ⸀γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.

verses.restored: This is the Moses who said to the children of Israel, The Divine will raise up for you a prophet like me from your siblings.

familiar.text: This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.

modern.text: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ ⸀εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ⸂ὁ θεὸς⸃ ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ.

verses.restored: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the messenger speaking to him on Mount Sinai and with our fathers, who received living oracles to give to us.

familiar.text: This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us:

modern.text: He was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. And he received living words to pass on to us. The Rebellion of Israel (Exodus 32:1–35; Deuteronomy 9:7–29; Amos 5:16–27)

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐδέξατο ⸀λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ⸀ἡμῖν,

verses.restored: Our fathers did not wish to become obedient to him, but pushed him away and turned in their hearts to Egypt,

familiar.text: To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt,

modern.text: But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.

original.text: ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ⸂ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις⸃ αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον,

verses.restored: saying to Aaron, Make us gods who will go before us; for this Moses who led us out from Egypt, we do not know what happened to him.

familiar.text: Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

modern.text: They said to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go before us! As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’

original.text: εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών· Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν· ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ⸀ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: They made a calf in those days and brought sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their hands.

familiar.text: And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

modern.text: At that time they made a calf and offered a sacrifice to the idol, rejoicing in the works of their hands.

original.text: καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ, καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: The Divine turned and gave them over to serve the host of heaven, just as it is written in the scroll of the prophets: Did you bring me slain beasts and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?

familiar.text: Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the prophets, O ye house of Israel, have ye offered to me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of forty years in the wilderness?

modern.text: But God turned away from them and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

original.text: ἔστρεψεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν· Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ;

verses.restored: You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the figures you made to worship; and I will relocate you beyond Babylon.

familiar.text: Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

modern.text: You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’ The Tabernacle of the Testimony (Exodus 40:1–33; Hebrews 9:1–10)

original.text: καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ ⸀Ῥαιφάν, τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς. καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος.

verses.restored: Our fathers had the tent of witness in the wilderness, just as the One speaking to Moses commanded him to make it according to the pattern he had seen.

familiar.text: Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, as he had appointed, speaking unto Moses, that he should make it according to the fashion that he had seen.

modern.text: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.

original.text: Ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἦν τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθὼς διετάξατο ὁ λαλῶν τῷ Μωϋσῇ ποιῆσαι αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸν τύπον ὃν ἑωράκει,

verses.restored: Receiving it in turn, our fathers brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations that the Divine drove out from the face of our fathers, until the days of David.

familiar.text: Which also our fathers that came after brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom God drave out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David;

modern.text: And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David,

original.text: ἣν καὶ εἰσήγαγον διαδεξάμενοι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν ἐξῶσεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἕως τῶν ἡμερῶν Δαυίδ·

verses.restored: David found grace before the Divine and asked to find a dwelling for the house of Jacob.

familiar.text: Who found favour before God, and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

modern.text: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

original.text: ὃς εὗρεν χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ᾐτήσατο εὑρεῖν σκήνωμα τῷ ⸀θεῷ Ἰακώβ.

verses.restored: But Solomon built him a house.

familiar.text: But Solomon built him an house.

modern.text: But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.

original.text: Σολομῶν δὲ οἰκοδόμησεν αὐτῷ οἶκον.

verses.restored: Yet the Most High does not dwell in handmade houses, just as the prophet says,

familiar.text: Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet,

modern.text: However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐχ ὁ ὕψιστος ἐν ⸀χειροποιήτοις κατοικεῖ· καθὼς ὁ προφήτης λέγει·

verses.restored: Heaven is my throne, and earth the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what is the place of my rest?

familiar.text: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build me? saith the Lord: or what is the place of my rest?

modern.text: ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?

original.text: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ⸂ἡ δὲ⸃ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου· ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, λέγει κύριος, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου;

verses.restored: Did not my hand make all these things?

familiar.text: Hath not my hand made all these things?

modern.text: Has not My hand made all these things?’

original.text: οὐχὶ ἡ χείρ μου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα πάντα;

verses.restored: Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the holy Spirit; as your fathers, so also you.

familiar.text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.

modern.text: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.

original.text: Σκληροτράχηλοι καὶ ἀπερίτμητοι ⸀καρδίαις καὶ τοῖς ὠσίν, ὑμεῖς ἀεὶ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε, ὡς οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ὑμεῖς.

verses.restored: Which of the prophets did your fathers not pursue? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers,

familiar.text: Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers:

modern.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers—

original.text: τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν; καὶ ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ δικαίου οὗ νῦν ὑμεῖς προδόται καὶ φονεῖς ⸀ἐγένεσθε,

verses.restored: you who received the Law by arrangements of messengers and did not guard it.

familiar.text: Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.

modern.text: you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.” The Stoning of Stephen

original.text: οἵτινες ἐλάβετε τὸν νόμον εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξατε.

verses.restored: Hearing these things, they were cut through in their hearts and were grinding their teeth at him.

familiar.text: When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.

modern.text: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.

original.text: Ἀκούοντες δὲ ταῦτα διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐπʼ αὐτόν.

verses.restored: But being full of holy Spirit, he looked intently into heaven and saw glory of the Divine and Jesus standing at the right hand of the Divine.

familiar.text: But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,

modern.text: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

original.text: ὑπάρχων δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶδεν δόξαν θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: He said, Look, I behold the heavens opened and the Son of Humanity standing at the right hand of the Divine.

familiar.text: And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

modern.text: “Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ⸀διηνοιγμένους καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Crying out with a great voice, they held their ears and rushed with one accord upon him.

familiar.text: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord,

modern.text: At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.

original.text: κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν, καὶ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπʼ αὐτόν,

verses.restored: Throwing him outside the city, they stoned him. The witnesses laid aside their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.

familiar.text: And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man’s feet, whose name was Saul.

modern.text: They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

original.text: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν. καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια ⸀αὐτῶν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας νεανίου καλουμένου Σαύλου.

verses.restored: They were stoning Stephen as he called out and said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

familiar.text: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

modern.text: While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”

original.text: καὶ ἐλιθοβόλουν τὸν Στέφανον ἐπικαλούμενον καὶ λέγοντα· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου·

verses.restored: Falling to his knees, he cried with a great voice, Lord, do not set this sin/misalignment against them. Saying this, he fell asleep.

familiar.text: And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

modern.text: Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

original.text: θεὶς δὲ τὰ γόνατα ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Κύριε, μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ⸂ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν⸃· καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐκοιμήθη.
